text.en:
1. (1) This Act may be cited as the Scouts Association of Malaysia
(Incorporation) Act 1968.

(2) This Act applies throughout Malaysia.

Interpretation

2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires—

"Council" means a Council constituted in accordance with the
rules of the Corporation referred to in section 6;

"Ordinance" means—

(a) the Boy Scouts Ordinance 1953 of the Federation of
Malaya [F.M. Ord. No. 60 of 1953);

(b) the Boy Scouts Association Ordinance of Sabah
[Sabah Cap. 17]; or

(c) the Boy Scouts Association Ordinance of Sarawak [Sarawak
Cap. 99);

"Scouts" includes Scout, Junior Scout, Senior Scout, Rover
Scout, Scouter, Lay Member of the Association or Member of
Baden-Powell Guild recognized by the Ordinance;

"Corporation" means the Persekutuan Pengakap-Pengakap
Malaysia or in English, the "Scouts Association of Malaysia"
incorporated by this Act;

"Association" means the Boy Scouts Association of Malaysia
referred to under the Ordinance.

Incorporation of Scouts Association of Malaysia

3. (1) Any person who, immediately before the commencement
of this Act, was a member of the Association and all Scouts who
become members of the Corporation pursuant to this Act or any
rules made under this Act shall be a body corporate by the name
of "Persekutuan Pengakap-Pengakap Malaysia" or in English, the
"Scouts Association of Malaysia" with perpetual succession.

(2) The Corporation may sue and be sued in its name and may
do all other matters and things incidental or appertaining to a
body corporate.

(3) The Corporation may —

(a) enter into contracts;

(b) acquire, purchase, take, hold and enjoy movable and
immovable property of every description; and

(c) convey, transfer, assign, surrender and yield up, charge,
mortgage, demise, reassign or otherwise dispose of, or
deal with, any movable or immovable property vested
in the Corporation,

upon such terms as the Corporation thinks fit.
Scouts Association of Malaysia (Incorporation) 7

Objects of Corporation

4. The objects of the Corporation are—

(a) to provide an organization which shall be open to all
Scouts in Malaysia to enable them to give effect to the
aim and purposes of the Corporation set out in section
5; and

(b) to do all other things as the Corporation or its Council
may deem incidental and conducive to the attainment
of such objects.

Aim and purposes of the Corporation

5. (1) The aim of the Corporation is to develop good citizenship
among boys by forming their character and to achieve this end

by—

(a) training them in habits of observation, obedience and
self-reliance;

(b) including loyalty and thoughtfulness for others;

(c) teaching them services useful to the public and handicrafts
useful to themselves; and

(d) promoting their physical, mental, and spiritual development.

(2) The principles and practice of the Corporation shall be based

on the Scout Promise and Scout Law and such other principles

and practice as shall be provided in the rules of the Corporation.
Council

6. The affairs of the Corporation shall be administered by a

Council to be constituted in accordance with the rules of the
Corporation.
Common seal

7. (1) The Corporation shall have a common seal and the seal may
be broken, changed, altered and made anew as the Corporation
thinks fit.

(2) All deeds, documents and other instruments requiring
the seal of the Corporation shall be sealed with the seal of
the Corporation pursuant to a resolution of the Council to the
effect, in the presence of the persons discharging the duties of
the National Chief Commissioner or an Assistant National Chief
Commissioner and one other person authorized by the Council
who shall sign every such deed, document or other instrument
to which such seal is affixed.

(3) The signing shall be sufficient evidence that the seal was
duly and properly affixed and that the seal is the lawful seal of
the Corporation.

Register of members

8. (1) The Council shall cause a register to be kept in which the
following particulars shall be recorded:

(a) the name of every Scout who immediately before the
commencement of this Act was a member of the
Association; or

(b) the name of every Scout who may thereafter become a
duly admitted member of the Corporation; and

(c) any other matters as may be determined by the Council.
(2) The register may be kept in such manner as the Council
may decide and the duty of keeping parts of the register may be
delegated to any member or official of the Corporation.
Rules and by-laws
9, It shall be lawful for the Council from time to time to make, alter

or revoke such rules as it may deem expedient for the management
of the affairs of the Corporation and the accomplishment of its
Scouts Association of Malaysia (Incorporation) 9

objects, and all rules and by-laws made shall be binding upon
the members of the Corporation.

Transfer of property and liabilities, etc.

10. (1) All property belonging immediately before the
commencement of this Act to the Association, whether held in
the name of the Chief Commissioner Boy Scouts Association
Federation of Malaya or in the name of any person in trust for
the Association shall be vested in the Corporation.

(2) All property mentioned in subsection (1) together with
all after-acquired property, movable or immovable, and all
subscriptions, contributions, donations, fines, amounts of loans
and advances received or to be received shall be held by the
Corporation for the purposes of this Act and subject to the rules
of the Corporation.

(3) All debts and liabilities of the Association existing
immediately before the commencement of this Act shall be paid
by the Corporation.

(4) All debts due to and subscriptions and contributions payable
to the Association immediately before the commencement of this
Act shall be paid to the Corporation.

Application of income and property

11. (1) The income and property of the Corporation, from whatever
place or source, shall be applied solely towards the promotion
of the objects of the Corporation as set out in this Act.

(2) No portion of the income and property of the Corporation
shall be paid or transferred directly or indirectly, by way of
dividend, bonus or otherwise by way of profit to the members
of the Corporation.

(3) Nothing in this section shall prevent the payment made
in good faith of remuneration to any officers or servants of the
Corporation or to any person in return for any services actually
rendered to the Corporation.

Restriction on sale of badges, efc., of the Association

12. No person, other than the Corporation or a person authorized
in writing so to do by the Corporation, shall sell or expose for
sale any badge, token or emblem specifically adopted for use by
a Scout under the rules of the Corporation.

Possession and restriction on use of badges

13. (1) No person, not being a Scout, shall publicly wear, carry
or bear in such a manner as to convey the impression that such
person is a Scout any badge, token or emblem specifically adopted
for use by a Scout under the rules of the Corporation.

(2) No person shall, without lawful authority or excuse, have
in his possession —

(a) any device which so closely resembles any badge, token
or emblem specifically adopted for use by a Scout under
the rules of the Corporation as to lead to the belief that
the device in question is such badge, token or emblem;

(b) any badge, token or emblem containing any words or
characters so closely resembling any words or characters
ordinarily used to describe any Scout as to be calculated
to deceive or mislead; or

(c) any badge, token or emblem bearing the word "Scout"
or "Scouts".

Penalty

14. Any person who contravenes any of the provisions of this
Act commits an offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a
fine not exceeding five hundred ringgit or to imprisonment for
a term not exceeding one month.
Scouts Association of Malaysia (Incorporation) 11
Repeal

15. The following laws are repealed:

(a) the Boy Scouts Ordinance 1953 of the Federation of
Malaya;

(b) the Boy Scouts Association Ordinance of Sabah; and

(c) the Boy Scouts Association Ordinance of Sarawak in so
far as the Ordinance apply to Boy Scouts.
